time adverb; part of A presto!

meanings.note: Unstressed 2nd-person plural object pronoun before a verb (vi chiedo, vi ricordo).

examples.trans: I remind you all of the rule.
I will wait for you all outside.

meanings.note: Vi ricordo che... ('I remind you all that...').

examples.trans: I remind you of the schedule.

meanings.note: Interrogative or exclamative word before verbs or nouns.
Conjunction or relative pronoun linking two clauses.

examples.trans: They say that it is true.

meanings.note: Standard negative particle placed immediately before the verb (plus any clitics).
Builds general statements (non si fuma, i copioni si cambiano).
Third-person reflexive pronoun (si chiama, si è svegliata, non si preoccupi).
Impersonal non si fuma is the standard Italian phrasing for 'no smoking'.
Contraction of preposition su + masculine singular article il (sul set, sul serio).
Invariable English borrowing universally used in Italian production.

examples.trans: There is no smoking on set.

meanings.note: Ordinal adjective; on a film slate, feminines prima / seconda stand for prima ripresa ('first take').

examples.text: Ho visto le prime due puntate.
examples.trans: I watched the first two episodes.

meanings.note: Familiar singular subject pronoun; darsi del tu means addressing each other informally.
Parlare con means speaking with someone; parlare male di means criticising.

examples.trans: I need to talk to you.

meanings.note: Follows a verb negated by non (non parli mai, 'you never speak').
Ordinal number; on set, seconda marks take two of a shot.
Introduces a condition (se vuoi, se ti va, se no 'otherwise').

examples.text: Se ti va, prendiamo un caffè.
examples.trans: If you fancy it, let us get a coffee.

meanings.note: Unstressed familiar 2nd-person singular direct, indirect, or reflexive pronoun.
Irregular verb; past participle detto, familiar imperative di' (fused in dille, 'tell her').
Indefinite article: un before most masculine nouns, uno before s + consonant/z, una (un') before feminine nouns.
General word for an object, statement, or situation.
Feminine singular definite article (la scena, la regia).
Third-person feminine singular direct object clitic (non la dico, la risolviamo).
Core verb used in many idioms: non fa niente, fare schifo, farsi la doccia, fare il bravo.
Links words or clauses; distinct from accented è, meaning is.
Third-person basta alone or in e basta means 'and that's it / enough'.

examples.trans: One coffee is enough for me.

meanings.note: Ordinal adjective/number after primo and secondo.
Identity, description, location, and passive/intransitive auxiliary; with ci forms c'è ('there is').
Both a mechanical machine (or tireless worker) and the everyday Italian word for car.
Small, darting animal; figuratively someone quick and tireless.

examples.trans: He darts around like a ferret.

stare.gloss: to stay; to be; to live

meanings.note: Stai fermo ('stay still'), stare in porta ('play in goal').
Come stai?, sto scherzando (stare + gerund for ongoing action), sta a Milano ('lives in Milan').

examples.trans: I am writing a note right now.

meanings.note: Adverbial counterpart of buono; in va bene it expresses agreement.
Variant of clitic ti required before lo, la, li, le, ne (te ne vai, te la senti, te l'ho detto).

examples.trans: Do you feel up to starting?

meanings.note: Partitive clitic replacing a counted noun (ne ho ventiquattro, 'I have twenty-four of them [years]').
Part of andarsene (te ne vai, 'you leave / walk away').

examples.text: Quanti anni hai? Ne ho venti.
examples.trans: How old are you? I am twenty.

meanings.note: Movement away from the speaker or toward a destination.
Used in expressions like va bene, ti va, or andare male.
First-person singular subject pronoun; usually included for contrast or emphasis.
Written with an accent to distinguish it from reflexive/impersonal pronoun si.

examples.trans: Yes, I am coming right away.

meanings.note: Negative pronoun; pairs with non before the verb (non vuoi niente, non fa niente).
Movement toward the speaker or listener (vieni con me, 'come with me').

examples.trans: On Sunday I am coming too.

meanings.note: Marks accompaniment, instrument, or attitude.
Stressed pronoun after prepositions (con me) and clitic form before li/lo/la/ne (me ne danno, me li sento).
Marks possession, material, department (stagista di regia), or topic.
Links verbs like dire, chiedere, pensare to a following infinitive.
Di che squadra sei? asks which football club someone supports.
Question word asking manner or requesting repetition (Come, scusa?).
Introduces a comparison.
Imperatives match address: scusa / scusami (informal tu), scusi (polite lei), scusate (plural voi).

examples.trans: Excuse me, where is the exit?

meanings.note: Contraction of di + feminine singular article la; after più, introduces comparison.
Also shouted as praise (Bravo! / Brava!); fare il bravo means to behave.
Irregular future vedrete ('you all will see') and past participle visto ('seen / watched').

examples.trans: Do you see those light stands?

meanings.note: Demonstrative determiner/pronoun; before masculine nouns adapts like lo/il: quel, quell', quello, quei, quegli.

examples.trans: Do you see those light stands?

meanings.note: Heavy metal tripod supporting studio lamps; takes lo / gli because it begins with st-.
Interrogative and relative adverb of place; elides to dov' before è.

examples.trans: Excuse me, where is the exit?

meanings.note: Third-person masculine plural direct object pronoun before the verb.
Modal verb followed directly by an infinitive.

examples.trans: I have to talk to you.

portare.gloss: to carry; to bring; to take

meanings.note: Portare a casa literally means carrying home, figuratively wrapping up a win or workday.

examples.trans: Where should I carry these chairs?
Let us bring the result home.

meanings.note: Negative reply; in se no ('if not'), means 'otherwise'.

examples.trans: Run, otherwise you will be late.

meanings.note: Takes a direct object without 'at'; guarda! draws someone's attention.

examples.trans: I have to watch the equipment.

meanings.note: Everyday counterpart of qui, often slightly broader ('around this place').
Plural rubano without a subject renders 'people steal'.
Singular tutto alone means 'everything'; masculine plural tutti alone means 'everyone'.
Sequences actions (e poi..., poi ti racconto); da oggi in poi means 'from today onwards'.

examples.trans: First we work, then we eat.
Later I will explain everything to you.

meanings.note: Everyday verb for making coffee or getting equipment ready.
Invariable cardinal number; sette e mezza means 7:30.
Invariable in the plural because it ends in a stressed vowel.
Marks beneficiary (per i ragazzi), duration/target (quanto per Corinna?), or reason (scusa per prima).
Default masculine plural definite article, plural of il.
Plural i ragazzi refers warmly to the team or crew.

examples.text: Prepara il caffè per i ragazzi.

meanings.note: Feminine noun also shouted before a team name as a cheer: Forza Roma!
Marks destination, location in cities, or indirect recipient.
Links activities and idioms such as giocare a tennis or a presto.
In A presto!, means 'see you soon!'.
